{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (IBM / MSL)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement, Statement of Work and ancillary agreements 
**Privileged and confidential — attorney work product**

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement and its attachments (Statement of Work, Attachment 6, Appendix A, the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement and the CI Agreement). On balance the document is favourable to us: intellectual property, indemnification, audit, warranty, exit assistance and pricing protections all run in our direction, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-purchase or liquidated-damages burden on us.

We identified **five items requiring attention** — four deviations and one missing clause:

- **Limitation of liability (critical).** The mutual cap of 3% of bill-of-materials value sits far below our fallback and, with no carve-outs, swallows MSL's IP indemnity and confidentiality obligations. This is walk-away territory as drafted.
- **Termination for convenience (high).** We have no mid-term exit across a committed three-year term; termination is available only for cause. Also walk-away territory.
- **Assignment (high).** A blanket consent requirement on our assignments, with no affiliate or successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard.
- **Auto-renewal (medium).** Non-renewal notice windows of six months (Base Agreement) and twelve months (SOW) — the latter longer than the six-month renewal period it governs.
- **Vendor insurance (low, missing).** No general liability, professional liability, cyber or workers' compensation covenant, despite MSL occupying our premises, holding our consigned inventory and accessing our networks and customer integration data.

We also flag two diligence items arising from redactions: the non-solicit duration in § 9.0(f), the warranty periods in § 19.1(a)(iv)–(v) and the return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) are all redacted in the copy reviewed and should be confirmed on the execution version.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15.3 Limitations of Liability |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property |
| 4 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term |
| 5 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 16.2 Assignment |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.3 Licenses |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.18 Restrictions and Limitations |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (and SOW Attachment § 2.0) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Attachment 1 |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 9.0 Personnel |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 5.2 Rights Upon Termination |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 Scope of Warranty |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 13.1 Consigned Products (nearest provision) |

---

## 3. Deviations and missing clause — detail and our proposals

### 3.1 Limitation of liability — § 15.3 (critical)

Section 15.3 contains a mutual cap and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, but the cap basis fails our fallback: 3% of the bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered over the entire term is far below twelve months' (or even six months') fees, so MSL's exposure is effectively illusory relative to the volume it manufactures for us. The cap is expressed as covering total liability "regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort," with no carve-outs — so MSL's § 15.1 indemnities (third-party IP infringement, regulatory non-compliance, warranty support) and its confidentiality obligations sit inside this very low cap with no super-cap.

**Proposal.** Reset the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and our payment obligations outside the cap. Mutuality is preserved, so the edit does not disturb the existing bargain beyond the cap basis and carve-outs.

### 3.2 Termination for convenience — § 4.0 / § 5.0 (high)

The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (§ 4.0, mirrored in SOW § 2.0) and § 5.0 permits termination only for cause — material breach, insolvency, change of control or force majeure (§ 5.1(a)–(c)). There is no right for us to terminate for convenience during the term; the only no-cause exit is a non-renewal notice that bites at the end of a term. The PO-level cancellation right in SOW § 6.1 lets us cancel individual Purchase Orders but does not provide an agreement-level exit and is subject to cost reimbursement. MSL likewise has no mid-term convenience right, so no vendor-side reciprocity issue arises.

**Proposal.** Add a new § 5.4 giving us a convenience right on 30 days' notice with refund of prepayments, preserving MSL's payment entitlements under §§ 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

### 3.3 Assignment — § 16.2 (high)

Section 16.2 imposes a blanket consent requirement on our assignments with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard on MSL's consent; the only reasonableness qualifier runs in MSL's favour for MSL Related Company assignments. This fails even the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice). Separately, there are no change-of-control provisions binding us — § 16.5 addresses only MSL's own sale or merger and requires the successor to assume performance — which is consistent with our preferred position.

**Proposal.** Amend the first sentence of § 16.2 to add an affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for us plus a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, leaving MSL's assignments consent-gated.

### 3.4 Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice — § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0 (medium)

Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows well beyond our 60-day fallback ceiling: § 4.0 requires six months' notice, and SOW Attachment § 2.0 requires twelve months' notice against a six-month renewal period — meaning notice must be given before the renewal period even begins.

**Proposal.** Shorten both windows to 30 days and align renewal periods at twelve months; a 60-day window remains acceptable as a fallback. Renewals continue on the same terms and conditions, so we are not pressing for a price-uplift cap or vendor reminder mechanic.

### 3.5 Vendor insurance — missing (low)

The Agreement contains no vendor insurance covenant. The only insurance references are property-specific: SOW § 13.1(b) (MSL replacement-value cover for our consigned Products, with us as joint insured), SOW § 21.2 (our obligation to insure our own tooling) and Loan Agreement § 8 (risk of loss on Loaned Items). None provides commercial general liability, professional liability, cyber/privacy or workers' compensation cover, so the document fails even our fallback. This matters because MSL occupies our premises, holds our and our customers' consigned inventory, and accesses our applications, networks and customer integration data under SOW § 24.1.

**Proposal.** Insert a new § 16.22 in the General section at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), expressly preserving the existing consigned-Products cover. Fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) can be offered in the covering comment.

---

## 4. Walk-away items

Two findings fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **§ 15.3 — cap with no carve-outs.** A 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap applying to MSL's IP indemnity and confidentiality obligations, with no super-cap, is the express walk-away scenario under LOL-CAP. We need, at minimum, carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, and confirmation that our payment obligations are not capped damages.
2. **§ 4.0 / § 5.0 — no convenience exit in a multi-year term.** "No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term" is walk-away under T4C. A 60–90 day notice period with a capped early-termination fee is our fallback landing zone.

The six- and twelve-month non-renewal windows in § 4.0 and SOW § 2.0 also exceed the 90-day walk-away threshold under RENEWAL, though we regard this as negotiable to the 30–60 day range rather than escalation-worthy in isolation.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the four deviations and the new insurance section: § 15.3 (cap basis and carve-outs), new § 5.4 (convenience termination), § 16.2 (affiliate/successor carve-out and reasonableness), § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0 (notice windows and renewal periods), and new § 16.22 (insurance). Comments to carry the `[Playbook]` prefix with fallbacks stated where noted above.
2. **Escalate the two walk-away items** (§ 15.3 and the absence of a convenience right) to the business sponsor before the next negotiation session, so we know our authority on the cap basis and any early-termination fee.
3. **Obtain the unredacted execution copy** and confirm three redacted figures: the non-solicit period in § 9.0(f) (walk-away above 24 months), the warranty durations in § 19.1(a)(iv)–(v) (we want at least twelve months for Products and Parts), and the confidential-information return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) (we prefer 30 days or less).
4. **Confirm the interaction of § 16.19** (sunset of representations and warranties on a stated anniversary of the Effective Date) with Product warranties on units delivered late in the term, so warranty cover is not cut short.
5. **Request the Lease of Premises Agreement** referenced at SOW § 10.0, which was not provided and may bear on premises-related insurance and risk allocation.
6. **Note for the record, not for redline:** the absence of an aggregate cap on the Appendix 2 forecast-accuracy true-up. We would pursue this only if the pricing appendices are reopened for other reasons.

No other provisions require amendment. The IP, indemnity, audit, warranty, exit-assistance, governing law, MFN, exclusivity, non-compete, licence-grant and minimum-commitment positions are compliant and, in several cases, better than our preferred position; we should resist any counterparty attempt to reopen them."}
